newsitem.title: UK: UK's Portillo pledges support for defence mergers.
newsitem.headline: UK's Portillo pledges support for defence mergers.

text.p: British Secretary of State for Defence Michael Portillo said on Monday the government would support joint ventures and mergers between UK and foreign defence companies if they were based on "industrial good sense."

In the text of a speech for delivery at the Confederation of British Industry annual conference here, Portillo said that as the defence industry in Europe and the U.S. restructured, "the government stands ready to offer its political support to companies entering joint ventures and mergers with foreign companies, provided these new arrangements are based on industrial good sense and on sustaining the competitiveness of British defence manufacturing capabilities."
Speaking to reporters, Portillo would not say if this meant the government would approve a merger between giants British Aerospace Plc and General Electric Co Plc.
"I wait for industry to put proposals before me and not the other way round," Portillo said.
Portillo said he hoped the German budget this week would allow Germany to play its part in the four-nation Eurofighter jet project, which involved Spain, Italy, Germany and Britain.
"I'm sure Eurofighter is not heading for the rocks," Portillo said, adding "We would greatly regret a delay to Eurofighter, which would be damaging but not fatal."
Portillo said a delay in the project would make the fighter aircraft "more expensive and damage its competitiveness."
